text:
incident-bot: Pager SEV2 — Canary cluster canary-west-2: 5xx spike and p95 latency up ~4x. Alerting at 2026-03-17T02:03:21Z. Link: https://telemetry.redwood/canary/abc123

Aisha (oncall): ack. I’m oncall and taking it. pulling up logs and recent deploy.

Tom (eng): I’m around — just checked the deploy diff. Small rollout included a toggle expansion for `zero_shot_cache` + a single commit that bumped k8s http-probe timeouts. PR: https://git.redwood/r/redwood/infra/pulls/4821

Aisha (oncall): seeing very high upstream `502` from model proxy on canaries, stack trace shows cache middleware throwing `KeyError` on prefix lookup. Repro on canary nodes only.

Tom (eng): ok that matches the toggle change. Recommend flip the toggle off for the canary cohort and revert the one commit if we still see failures. We can also push a minimal patch to guard the cache lookup.

sre-bridge: running emergency toggle command now for canary cluster:
```bash
./infra/flags set --env=prod --cluster=canary-west-2 --flag=zero_shot_cache --value=false --reason="canary 5xx spike"
```

Aisha (oncall): toggle applied. K8s rolling restart not required. Watching metrics.

Kyle (support): customers reporting degraded responses for a small subset of requests — volume low but visible. I pushed a note to status: https://status.redwood/incident/INC-2026-045

(2m later) Tom (eng): preliminary metrics: 5xx rate down ~60% on the canary nodes that got the toggle flip. But a small tail of errors persists. I have a 1-line guard I can hotpatch and release (single-commit revert approach ready) — will open the PR and request urgent review.

Tom (eng): PR opened: https://git.redwood/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/4830 — revert of commit `f3b9c2d` + safe-nil-check for cache lookup. Build artifacts: `canary-hotfix-20260317-01`

Aisha (oncall): approving the quick patch to canary. Please proceed with canary-only deploy and hold for 5m.

Tom (eng): deploying canary-hotfix now via `./deploy canary --artifact=canary-hotfix-20260317-01`

sre-bridge: deploy started. Tracking: https://deploys.redwood/canary-hotfix-20260317-01

(5m later) incident-bot: Canary deploy succeeded. Health checks green. 5xx back to baseline. p95 latency returned to normal.

Aisha (oncall): confirming observability — top-level SLI returned to normal on canary-west-2. No new customer reports in last 10m.

Kyle (support): I posted an update to affected customers and cleared the high-severity tag. Will monitor for inbound tickets.

Jenna (product): thanks team. For postmortem: can we capture why the toggle expansion wasn't gated and add a preflight check that rejects toggles that change cache shape without schema compatibility?

Tom (eng): +1. Action items: 1) Add preflight toggle compatibility check (owner: eng-runtime) 2) Add canary gating rule to run small synthetic through new toggle (owner: eng-sre) 3) Backfill a unit test for cache lookup nil-safety (owner: eng-ml).

Aisha (oncall): handing off to morning oncall @Tom (eng) for follow-up and postmortem writeup. I’ll stay available for questions.

Tom (eng): I’ll take it. Creating incident doc and scheduling postmortem in #postmortems. Tentative RCA: toggle expanded cache semantics + missing nil-guard => KeyError under certain prefix cases on canary traffic.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-045 updated: status -> mitigated. Oncall handover recorded. Next steps: postmortem due in 3 business days.

Aisha (oncall): closing pager. leaving final note: quick toggle + single-commit hotpatch avoided full rollback. We still need to tighten toggle rollout playbook. :white_check_mark:
